1.title: The Cloud Native Ecosystem and Community
1.text: Welcome to Module 14: The Cloud Native Ecosystem and Community. This module is in the Cloud Native Architecture domain, and it covers the topic called Community and Collaboration. By the end you will be able to do four things. Describe the C N C F bodies: the Governing Board, the T O C, T A Gs, T C Gs and the end user community. Order the maturity levels: sandbox, incubating, graduated, and know archived. Explain S I Gs, working groups and K E Ps in the Kubernetes community. And name the next exams after the K C N A.

1.title: Case Check-In: Harbor Books Joins the Community
1.text: At Harbor Books, the team relies on open source projects from the C N C F landscape, and wants to judge how mature a project is before adopting it. One engineer wants to report a bug and propose a small change to Kubernetes. A developer asks which exam to take after the K C N A. In this module you learn who governs the ecosystem, and how to take part.

1.title: The CNCF and Its Bodies
1.text: This slide is tagged moving. Its mission is ubiquitous cloud native computing, through open source, vendor-neutral projects. The Governing Board sets the budget and the business direction. The T O C, the Technical Oversight Committee, is the technical body. It admits, oversees and archives projects. T A Gs, technical advisory groups, and T C Gs, technical community groups, gather experts around topics. And the end user community speaks for the people who use C N C F projects. As of the thirtieth of October, twenty twenty-six, there are five T A Gs, and four T C Gs, and earlier T A Gs were archived. Exam tip: the board is business, the T O C is technology, and end users bring needs.

1.title: Project Maturity and the Landscape
1.text: This slide is tagged moving. Projects have maturity levels. Sandbox projects are experimental, and not yet widely tested in production. Incubating projects are used successfully in production by a small number of users, with a healthy pool of contributors. Graduated projects are stable, widely adopted and production ready. And archived projects have reached the end of their lifecycle and become inactive. The C N C F landscape is a map of cloud native projects and products. As of the thirtieth of October, twenty twenty-six, thirty-nine projects are graduated, including Kubernetes, Prometheus, Open Telemetry, Argo, Flux and Helm. Exam tip: sandbox, incubating, graduated. Archived is the end of the road.

1.title: The Kubernetes Community
1.text: The Kubernetes community has several kinds of groups. A S I G, a Special Interest Group, is a persistent, open group that owns a part of the project and its subprojects. A working group is temporary, and handles an issue that crosses S I G boundaries. It owns no code. A committee is chartered for sensitive topics, such as the steering committee or the code of conduct. A K E P, a Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal, tracks a new feature through alpha, beta and stable. And the Release Team runs each release cycle. Anyone may take part if they follow the Code of Conduct. Kube Con plus Cloud Native Con is the community conference. Exam tip: S I Gs own areas, working groups cross them, and K E Ps plan features.

1.title: From the KCNA to the Next Exams
1.text: This slide is tagged moving. The K C N A is a multiple choice exam of ninety minutes, with no prerequisites, valid for two years. The K C S A is the cloud native security associate exam, also multiple choice, ninety minutes, with no prerequisites. The C K A, the C K A D and the C K S are performance-based. You solve tasks in a command line. The C K A is the administrator exam, and takes two hours. The C K A D is for application developers. The C K S is for security specialists, and you must pass the C K A first. As of the thirtieth of October, twenty twenty-six, the Linux Foundation suggests the K C S A or the C K A as the next step. Exam tip: K C N A and K C S A are multiple choice, and C K A, C K A D and C K S are hands-on.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: To recap. The C N C F mission is vendor-neutral open source. The Governing Board is business, the T O C is technology, T A Gs and T C Gs advise, and end users bring needs. The maturity levels are sandbox, incubating and graduated, with archived at the end of life, and the landscape maps the field. In Kubernetes, S I Gs own areas, working groups cross S I Gs, K E Ps plan features, and the Release Team ships them. You take part through the Code of Conduct, the contributor guide and Kube Con plus Cloud Native Con. And the next exams are the K C S A and the C K A, then the C K A D and the C K S. Now three practice questions.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Which C N C F body is the technical governing body that admits and oversees projects? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The T O C is the technical decision body of the C N C F. The Governing Board handles budget and business direction, the End User T A B speaks for users, and T C Gs and T A Gs are community and advisory groups.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Harbor Books wants a project that is stable, widely adopted and production ready. Which C N C F maturity level describes such a project? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Graduated projects are stable, widely adopted and production ready. Incubating projects have a smaller base of production users, sandbox projects are experimental, and archived projects are at the end of their lifecycle.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What is the difference between a Kubernetes S I G and a working group? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. A S I G is a persistent, open group that owns a part of the project and its subprojects. A working group is temporary and addresses issues that cross S I G boundaries, and it owns no code. Committees handle sensitive topics.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are the answers at a glance. Question one, D: the T O C admits and oversees projects. Question two, A: graduated means stable, widely adopted and production ready. Question three, C: a S I G is persistent, and a working group is temporary.
